trust_boundary: the verifier issuance registry and all private registries are SAME-PROCESS API CAPABILITY DISCIPLINE: ordinary API callers cannot manufacture an accepted receipt without the verifier issuance path. This is NOT cryptographic isolation and NOT hostile-code isolation -- introspection inside the same Python process is out of scope by design (RC-0.4 section 7).
self_reference_law: This receipt records the PARENT commit and the code-tree digest; the commit SHA that contains this receipt can only be bound by a follow-up commit. Any such binding record is an UNSIGNED Git-history binding, not a signed or independently verified attestation, until the owner signs with a real key.

mutation_audit.mechanism: disposable working copy per mutation (scratch tree; original package never modified; pristine digests verified before/after); CAUGHT requires the named test to fail with an AssertionError -- the semantic law's own assertion -- not an incidental crash

mutation_status_law.law: stale report deleted before launch; only a fresh report from the current tree with exit 0 and every mutation applied AND caught by a semantic AssertionError is accepted; a crash never falls back to prior evidence

mutation_manifest_law.law: the fresh report must contain EXACTLY the frozen mutation set (names, count, file/test pairs); a missing, extra, renamed, or re-targeted mutation REFUTES the status (RC-0.4A section 4)

digest_domain: all artifact digests are SHA-256 over RAW FILE BYTES exactly as stored on disk (no newline normalization, no encoding transform); trace/seal digests are SHA-256 over canonical JSON (sorted keys, ensure_ascii, compact separators)
claims_permitted: the deterministic reference controller enforces its typed authority, verification, and seal semantics across every registered path, and detects all eight injected attacks
